messages:
maria.g: Heads up — noticed ~12 users lost their org roles after SSO logins this morning. They were JIT-provisioned by Okta but the role mapping depends on the `department` attribute which was missing in the assertion. Logs below show mapping returned empty and JIT created accounts with no roles.

jonathan: :eyes: which mapping specifically? attribute->role or group->role?

maria.g: attribute->role. We map SAML attribute `department` to internal role names (eg `product` -> `product-engineer`). If `department` is absent we currently do not apply any fallback.

sam: I reproduced this locally by stripping `department` from the assertion. quick dump: ```
<saml:AttributeStatement>
  <!-- department attribute intentionally missing -->
  <saml:Attribute Name="email">team@redwood.ai</saml:Attribute>
</saml:AttributeStatement>
```

lena: Okta admin UI shows a recent tweak to the app attribute release policy yesterday (cleanup of custom claims). @ashwin did you run a bulk attribute rewrite?

ashwin: I removed an unused transformation rule that referenced `user.department` for some auto-provisioned groups — thought it was dead. Looks like for these users the upstream identity provider didn't populate `department` and Okta was relying on the transform. I can revert.

maria.g: Impact summary: ~12 users in two teams couldn't access dashboards that require `product-engineer` role. No privilege escalation observed, only missing permissions. Audit shows failed role assignment events.

security-oncall: Noted. This looks like a regression in attribute mapping and lack of a safe fallback in JIT. I opened a tracking incident in the incident channel. Please include audit IDs when you have them.

sam: sample auth service log: ```
2025-11-05T14:22:03Z INFO  auth.jit ProvisionUser uid=U12345 source=okta assertion_id=A-9876 attrs_present=[email] attrs_missing=[department] mapped_roles=[]
2025-11-05T14:22:03Z WARN  auth.jit Created user without roles uid=U12345
```

okta-bot: Okta audit: application.update by lena.admin at 2025-11-05T14:20:11Z (change id: OKT-4421)

sre-bot: incident created INC-1423; priority=P2; assigned=security; link=#incidents-1423

jonathan: Short-term mitigation options: 1) revert the Okta attribute change (if safe) 2) change JIT mapping to apply a default role like `employee` or `viewer` when `department` missing 3) run a remediation script to reassign expected roles for affected users (we can infer role from Okta group membership).

ashwin: I'll revert the transform and push a small JIT fallback: if `department` missing, consult `okta.groups` mapping -> then fallback to `viewer`. Rolling change to auth.jit mapping in 30m. After revert I'll run a remediation that re-evaluates users who were created between 2025-11-05T14:15 and 2025-11-05T14:45.

maria.g: Can you also emit audit events for fallback decisions? Right now logs just say `mapped_roles=[]`. We need `mapped_roles=[fallback:viewer]` so security/audit can see decisions.

ashwin: Good call. Adding explicit audit field `fallback_role` and reason. Will include KMS-signed event id for audit immutability.

security-oncall: Impact classification: access-loss (non-elevating). Postmortem checklist: root cause, detection time, why attribute removal was allowed, missing fallback policy, remediation timeline, rollout of hardened mapping, audit events and reassign script. Owner: ashwin. ETA for hotfix + remediation: 2h.

lena: +1. I'll coordinate with Okta admin team to revert the attribute release change and run a tighter review for attribute transforms.

maria.g: Action items: 
- ashwin: revert okta transform + deploy JIT fallback (owner)
- sam: run remediation script and report list of impacted users (owner)
- lena: follow up with Okta admins and document change (owner)
- security-oncall: capture audit event IDs and publish preliminary incident note (owner)

ashwin: Starting revert now, posting progress.``
